mainEntity.name: Can teeth grinding cause permanent damage to my teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Over time, untreated bruxism may cause noticeable enamel wear, increased tooth sensitivity, and in some cases, cracks or chips in the teeth. Existing dental restorations such as crowns or fillings may also be affected. However, with early identification and appropriate management — such as the use of a custom-made occlusal splint — the risk of significant damage can be reduced. Your dentist can assess the extent of any wear and recommend suitable protective or restorative options based on your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I grind my teeth at night?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nocturnal bruxism can be difficult to self-diagnose because it occurs during sleep. Common indicators include waking with a sore jaw, morning headaches, or facial muscle tenderness. A partner may also notice grinding sounds during the night. Your dentist can identify physical signs of grinding during a routine examination, such as flattened tooth surfaces or patterns of enamel wear. If you suspect you may be grinding your teeth, discussing your symptoms with a dental professional is a helpful first step.

mainEntity.name: Are over-the-counter night guards effective for bruxism?

acceptedAnswer.text: Over-the-counter mouth guards may offer some degree of protection; however, they are not custom-fitted and may be less comfortable, potentially affecting sleep quality. A custom-made occlusal splint, fabricated by your dentist from precise impressions of your teeth, provides a more accurate fit, better protection, and greater comfort. Your dentist can advise whether a custom appliance would be appropriate for your situation based on the severity of your bruxism and any existing dental concerns.

Yes, teeth grinding can occur in children as well as adults. It is relatively common in younger children and may be related to the development of their teeth and jaws. In many cases, childhood bruxism resolves naturally as the child grows. However, if a child is experiencing jaw pain, headaches, or noticeable tooth wear, it is advisable to mention this to their dentist during a routine appointment so that the situation can be monitored.

mainEntity.name: Will reducing stress definitely stop my teeth grinding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stress management can be a very effective component of bruxism management, particularly when stress or anxiety is a primary contributing factor. However, bruxism may have multiple causes, and reducing stress alone may not fully resolve the condition in every case. A comprehensive approach — combining stress reduction with dental protective measures — tends to be the most effective strategy. Your dentist can help identify the factors most relevant to your situation.

mainEntity.name: Is bruxism linked to other health conditions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bruxism has been associated with several other conditions, including sleep apnoea, gastro-oesophageal reflux, and certain anxiety disorders. Some medications, particularly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), have also been linked to an increased risk of teeth grinding. If you are concerned about a possible connection between bruxism and another health condition or medication, it is advisable to discuss this with both your dentist and your GP for a coordinated approach to management.
